events.title: Creation
events.summary: God makes the world and the first people, and calls it good.
events.yearNote: No calendar year in the text.
context: God makes the world and the first people, and calls it good.
events.kidNote: Read-aloud for every age. Stay with the chapter.

events.title: The Fall
events.summary: Adam and Eve disobey, and death and exile enter the story.
events.yearNote: No year in the text.
context: Adam and Eve disobey, and death and exile enter the story.
events.kidNote: Short and plain.

events.title: The Flood
events.summary: God judges a violent world, saves Noah's family in the ark, and promises not to flood the earth again.
events.yearNote: No year in the text.
context: God judges a violent world, saves Noah's family in the ark, and promises not to flood the earth again.
events.kidNote: Keep the telling at Genesis's level.

events.title: The Tower of Babel
events.summary: People try to make a name for themselves in one city. God confuses their language and scatters them.
events.yearNote: Do not equate the tower with a named ziggurat.
context: People try to make a name for themselves in one city. God confuses their language and scatters them.
events.kidNote: Scripture, not an archaeology unit.

events.title: God calls Abram from Ur
events.summary: God calls Abram to leave his country, promising blessing to all nations through him.
events.yearNote: No year. Leave secular chronologies unnamed.
context: God calls Abram to leave his country, promising blessing to all nations through him.

events.title: Khufu and the Great Pyramid
events.summary: Pharaoh Khufu builds the Great Pyramid at Giza as his tomb.
events.yearNote: Conventional Egyptology. Britannica: Khufu, 4th dynasty (c. 2543–c. 2436 BCE), Great Pyramid completed in the early 25th century BCE. Not a biblical date.
context: Pharaoh Khufu builds the Great Pyramid at Giza as his tomb.
events.kidNote: Burial, not horror. Do not connect Khufu to Joseph or Moses.

events.title: Joseph in Egypt
events.summary: Joseph is sold into Egypt, rises to serve Pharaoh, and brings his family there through the famine.
events.yearNote: Genesis names no pharaoh.
context: Joseph is sold into Egypt, rises to serve Pharaoh, and brings his family there through the famine.
events.kidNote: Slavery and prison are in the text. Keep it there.

events.title: Israel enslaved in Egypt
events.summary: A later pharaoh fears Israel's growth and forces them into hard labor.
events.yearNote: No pharaoh is named.
context: A later pharaoh fears Israel's growth and forces them into hard labor.
events.kidNote: Serious, not graphic.

events.title: Moses and the Exodus
events.summary: God calls Moses, sends the plagues, and brings Israel out of Egypt through the sea.
events.yearNote: No pharaoh and no modern year. Early-date and late-date theories are not picked.
context: God calls Moses, sends the plagues, and brings Israel out of Egypt through the sea.
events.kidNote: Tell the plagues straight, without extra gore.

events.title: Which pharaoh was it?
events.summary: This timeline does not decide which pharaohs match Joseph or the Exodus.
events.yearNote: Left open.
context: This timeline does not decide which pharaohs match Joseph or the Exodus.
This is an interpretation, not a settled fact.
events.kidNote: For 11 and 13, with a parent.

events.title: Sinai and the law
events.summary: At Sinai, God gives Israel the law, including the Ten Commandments.
context: At Sinai, God gives Israel the law, including the Ten Commandments.

events.title: Joshua and the land
events.summary: Joshua leads Israel into the land.
context: Joshua leads Israel into the land.

events.title: The judges
events.summary: Before the kings, judges lead Israel, and Ruth's story sits in those days.
context: Before the kings, judges lead Israel, and Ruth's story sits in those days.

events.title: Saul, David, and Solomon
events.summary: Saul, David, and Solomon rule Israel.
context: Saul, David, and Solomon rule Israel.

events.title: The divided kingdom
events.summary: After Solomon, the kingdom splits into Israel and Judah.
context: After Solomon, the kingdom splits into Israel and Judah.

events.title: Athens and Sparta
events.summary: Athens and Sparta led different ways of life through the great conflicts of classical Greece.
events.yearNote: Century, not a single year.
context: Athens and Sparta led different ways of life through the great conflicts of classical Greece.

events.title: Exile in Babylon
events.summary: Babylon takes many people of Judah away from Jerusalem.
context: Babylon takes many people of Judah away from Jerusalem.

events.title: Return and the walls
events.summary: Exiles return, and Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls.
context: Exiles return, and Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls.

events.title: Battle of Thermopylae
events.summary: A small Greek force led by Leonidas held the pass against Xerxes for three days.
events.yearNote: August 480 BCE, World History Encyclopedia.
context: A small Greek force led by Leonidas held the pass against Xerxes for three days.
events.kidNote: Deaths in battle. Keep it high-level.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.summary: Greek ships defeated the larger Persian fleet near Salamis.
events.yearNote: Same year, from the World History Encyclopedia Thermopylae article's account of the Persian Wars.
context: Greek ships defeated the larger Persian fleet near Salamis.

events.title: Alexander's campaigns
events.summary: Alexander of Macedon conquered from Greece through Egypt and Persia toward India.
events.yearNote: Reign; died June 323 BCE.
context: Alexander of Macedon conquered from Greece through Egypt and Persia toward India.
events.kidNote: Conquest. Century-level for younger listeners.

events.title: Hellenistic age
events.summary: Alexander's generals ruled successor kingdoms, and Greek language spread across the Near East.
events.yearNote: After Alexander until 31 BCE, World History Encyclopedia.
context: Alexander's generals ruled successor kingdoms, and Greek language spread across the Near East.

events.title: Greek myths
events.summary: Stories of the gods, heroes, and Troy. Cultural literacy, not Scripture.
events.yearNote: Literature, not history.
context: Stories of the gods, heroes, and Troy. Cultural literacy, not Scripture.
This is an interpretation, not a settled fact.
events.kidNote: Age-gate. Pagan religion, some violence.

events.title: Augustus and the early Roman Empire
events.summary: Rome under Augustus ruled a vast Mediterranean world.
events.yearNote: Century framing for the world the Gospel entered.
context: Rome under Augustus ruled a vast Mediterranean world.

events.title: Jesus: birth, ministry, death, and resurrection
events.summary: Jesus is born, teaches, dies on the cross, and rises.
events.yearNote: No civil year assigned.
context: Jesus is born, teaches, dies on the cross, and rises.
events.kidNote: Tell the crucifixion truthfully, without graphic detail for little ones.

events.title: Pentecost and the apostles
events.summary: The Spirit is given, and the apostles preach Christ from Jerusalem outward.
events.yearNote: No invented years.
context: The Spirit is given, and the apostles preach Christ from Jerusalem outward.

events.title: Persecution under Rome
events.summary: Some Christians suffered for refusing to worship the emperor or the Roman gods.
events.yearNote: A century band. Martyr stories vary.
context: Some Christians suffered for refusing to worship the emperor or the Roman gods.
events.kidNote: Preview martyr chapters before reading them aloud.

events.title: Roman virtue stories
events.summary: Stories such as Horatius, Cincinnatus, and Regulus, as later ages remembered Roman courage.
events.yearNote: Later retellings, not a chronicle.
context: Stories such as Horatius, Cincinnatus, and Regulus, as later ages remembered Roman courage.
This is an interpretation, not a settled fact.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.summary: Romulus Augustulus was deposed, and the Western Empire's political power ended.
events.yearNote: Conventional date for the fall of the West. The Eastern Empire continued.
context: Romulus Augustulus was deposed, and the Western Empire's political power ended.
events.kidNote: One sentence for young kids.

events.title: The Middle Ages in the West
events.summary: New kingdoms rose in Europe, and the Christian faith kept shaping the culture.
events.yearNote: Hinge at the fall of the West.
context: New kingdoms rose in Europe, and the Christian faith kept shaping the culture.

events.title: Magna Carta
events.summary: English barons forced King John to accept a charter limiting royal power.
events.yearNote: Usual date. World History Encyclopedia has a Magna Carta page; that page was not fully re-read this pass, so treat 1215 as the standard year, not a fresh line-check.
context: English barons forced King John to accept a charter limiting royal power.

events.title: Wycliffe and the English Bible
events.summary: John Wycliffe argued that ordinary people should have the Bible in their own language.
events.yearNote: World History Encyclopedia Reformation article: Wycliffe lived about 1330–1384.
context: John Wycliffe argued that ordinary people should have the Bible in their own language.
events.kidNote: The novel about him is fiction. The event is not.

events.title: Gutenberg's press
events.summary: Gutenberg's press made books, including Bibles, far more available.
events.yearNote: Movable metal type in Europe in the 1450s; Gutenberg Bible 1456.
context: Gutenberg's press made books, including Bibles, far more available.

events.title: Luther's Ninety-Five Theses
events.summary: Luther challenged the sale of indulgences, and the Reformation followed.
events.yearNote: Usual start of the Protestant Reformation on the World History Encyclopedia timeline.
context: Luther challenged the sale of indulgences, and the Reformation followed.
events.kidNote: Doctrine stays parent-led.

events.title: The Reformation era
events.summary: Reform movements reshaped churches and nations, with long religious and political conflict.
events.yearNote: World History Encyclopedia's usual span, through the Peace of Westphalia.
context: Reform movements reshaped churches and nations, with long religious and political conflict.
events.kidNote: Wars and martyrdom. Honest, not graphic.

events.title: King Arthur legends
events.summary: Arthur stories are literature of chivalry, not verified history.
events.yearNote: Romance, not a chronicle.
context: Arthur stories are literature of chivalry, not verified history.
This is an interpretation, not a settled fact.
events.kidNote: Children's versions only.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
events.summary: Columbus, sailing for Spain, reached islands in the Bahamas.
events.yearNote: Landfall 12 October 1492.
context: Columbus, sailing for Spain, reached islands in the Bahamas.
events.kidNote: Later voyages brought colonization and harm. Say so, without gore.

events.title: The Pilgrims in New England
events.summary: English Separatists sailed to plant a colony where they could worship freely.
events.yearNote: Mayflower colony, from the Landing of the Pilgrims recommendations. Not a day-by-day trivia list.
context: English Separatists sailed to plant a colony where they could worship freely.

events.title: Galileo and Newton
events.summary: Galileo and Newton changed how Europe studied the heavens and natural laws.
events.yearNote: Century band.
context: Galileo and Newton changed how Europe studied the heavens and natural laws.
events.kidNote: Skip deep-time asides in some biographies.

events.title: The American Revolution
events.summary: Thirteen British colonies fought for independence and formed the United States.
events.yearNote: The war years, century-level is fine for young kids.
context: Thirteen British colonies fought for independence and formed the United States.
events.kidNote: War. High-level for the young ones.

events.title: The Constitution
events.summary: Delegates write the Constitution of the United States.
context: Delegates write the Constitution of the United States.

events.title: Louisiana Purchase and Lewis and Clark
events.summary: The United States buys the Louisiana territory, and Lewis and Clark travel west.
events.yearNote: 1803 is the purchase. Journey years were not separately re-checked.
context: The United States buys the Louisiana territory, and Lewis and Clark travel west.

events.title: Battle of Waterloo
events.summary: Allied armies defeated Napoleon, ending the Napoleonic Wars.
events.yearNote: World History Encyclopedia.
context: Allied armies defeated Napoleon, ending the Napoleonic Wars.
events.kidNote: Summary only.

events.title: Slavery and abolition
events.summary: People are held in slavery in America, and others work to end it.
events.yearNote: Emancipation Proclamation as the anchor. The struggle is longer.
context: People are held in slavery in America, and others work to end it.

events.title: Overland trails west
events.summary: Families travel west by wagon.
events.yearNote: Setting year of Bound for Oregon.
context: Families travel west by wagon.

events.title: Textile mills
events.summary: Textile mills change how cloth is made and how people work.
events.yearNote: Century band from SCM's Mill.
context: Textile mills change how cloth is made and how people work.

events.title: Brooklyn Bridge
events.summary: New York builds the Brooklyn Bridge.
context: New York builds the Brooklyn Bridge.

events.title: Child labor and Lewis Hine
events.summary: Children work in factories. Lewis Hine photographs them.
events.yearNote: Late 19th and early 20th century. No single year.
context: Children work in factories. Lewis Hine photographs them.

events.title: The American Civil War
events.summary: The United States fought a civil war, at terrible human cost.
events.yearNote: The war that ended slavery and preserved the Union.
context: The United States fought a civil war, at terrible human cost.
events.kidNote: No gore. Say that many died and families were divided.

events.title: World War I
events.summary: A great war engulfed Europe and beyond.
events.yearNote: World History Encyclopedia, causes article.
context: A great war engulfed Europe and beyond.
events.kidNote: Age-fit books only.

events.title: World War II
events.summary: A worldwide war ended with Allied victory.
events.yearNote: Standard dating of the war.
context: A worldwide war ended with Allied victory.
events.kidNote: The Holocaust and other atrocities are true. Age-gate them. No graphic detail.

events.title: The American civil rights struggle
events.summary: Americans confronted racial injustice. The stories worth telling are about dignity and courage.
events.yearNote: Century, not a partisan timeline.
context: Americans confronted racial injustice. The stories worth telling are about dignity and courage.
events.kidNote: Parent guidance.

events.title: Apollo 11
events.summary: A huge team landed astronauts on the moon and brought them home.
events.yearNote: Moon landing.
context: A huge team landed astronauts on the moon and brought them home.

events.title: Modern church witness
events.summary: Christians kept preaching and serving, and some suffered under dictators.
events.yearNote: Missions and courage under tyranny, not one dated incident.
context: Christians kept preaching and serving, and some suffered under dictators.
events.kidNote: Preview persecution chapters.
